sentences.text: Lucius magister est. Hodie in schola est. Pueri et puellae in schola sunt. Marcus quoque in schola est.
sentences.english: Lucius is a teacher. Today he is at school. The boys and girls are at school. Marcus is at school too.

sentences.text: Lucius dicit: Salvete, pueri!
sentences.english: Lucius says: Hello, boys!

sentences.text: Quomodo valetis? Estisne fessi?
sentences.english: How are you? Are you tired?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Non sumus fessi, magister. Bene valemus.
sentences.english: We are not tired, teacher. We are well.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Bene! Nunc audite! Habetisne libros?
sentences.english: Good! Now listen! Do you have books?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Libros habemus. Sed librum meum non habeo.
sentences.english: We have books. But I do not have my book.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Lucius Marcum videt. Marcus librum non habet.
sentences.english: Lucius sees Marcus. Marcus does not have a book.

sentences.text: Quaere, Marce!
sentences.english: Look, Marcus!
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Quaero in mensa. Non est in mensa! Quaero in schola. Non est in schola! Non invenio!
sentences.english: I look on the table. It is not on the table! I look in the school. It is not in the school! I do not find it!
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Puella Marcum videt. Puella librum habet.
sentences.english: A girl sees Marcus. The girl has the book.

sentences.text: Ecce, Marce! Hic est! Invenio!
sentences.english: Look, Marcus! Here it is! I find it!
sentences.speaker: puella

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago! Tu amica bona es.
sentences.english: Thank you! You are a good friend.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Libenter tibi do.
sentences.english: I give it to you gladly.
sentences.speaker: puella

sentences.text: Bene est. Nunc audite, omnes!
sentences.english: It is well. Now listen, all!
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Omnes audiunt. Lucius dicit: Quid est hoc? Estne panis? Estne aqua?
sentences.english: All listen. Lucius says: What is this? Is it bread? Is it water?

sentences.text: Pueri dicunt: Aqua est! Marcus dicit: Panis est!
sentences.english: The boys say: It is water! Marcus says: It is bread!

sentences.text: Magister dicit: Bene! Nunc quaerite panem!
sentences.english: The teacher says: Good! Now look for bread!

sentences.text: Omnes quaerunt. Marcus panem et aquam invenit.
sentences.english: All look. Marcus finds bread and water.

sentences.text: Quid habes, Marce?
sentences.english: What do you have, Marcus?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Aquam habeo, magister. Et panem habeo. Martha panem vendit. Panis bonus est.
sentences.english: I have water, teacher. And I have bread. Martha sells bread. The bread is good.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Et tu? Quid habes?
sentences.english: And you? What do you have?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Lac habeo, magister. Et vinum non habeo.
sentences.english: I have milk, teacher. And I do not have wine.
sentences.speaker: puella

sentences.text: Bene! Gratias vobis ago, pueri. Hodie bene valetis.
sentences.english: Good! Thank you, boys. Today you are well.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Cras in foro sum. Panem emo, et lac emo. Quis panem vendit?
sentences.english: Tomorrow I am in the market. I buy bread, and I buy milk. Who sells bread?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Martha panem vendit, et lac vendit. Martha bona est.
sentences.english: Martha sells bread, and she sells milk. Martha is good.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Bene! Cras Marthae gratias ago. Panem et lac emo.
sentences.english: Good! Tomorrow I thank Martha. I buy bread and milk.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Ubi est Anna? Estne in schola?
sentences.english: Where is Anna? Is she at school?
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Anna in schola non est. In valetudinario est.
sentences.english: Anna is not at school. She is at the clinic.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Anna soror mea est. Anna bona est, et ego Annam amo.
sentences.english: Anna is my sister. Anna is good, and I love Anna.
sentences.speaker: luis

sentences.text: Hodie in schola omnes bene valent. Lucius fessus non est. Marcus fessus non est.
sentences.english: Today at school all are well. Lucius is not tired. Marcus is not tired.
